saints.name: St. Peter Canisius
saints.title: Priest and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The Jesuit catechist called the Second Apostle of Germany, whose catechisms held countless souls to the faith…
biography: Born at Nijmegen on 8 May 1521, the son of the city's burgomaster, Peter Kanis studied at Cologne and, won by the direction of Peter Faber, entered the young Society of Jesus in 1543 — the first Dutchman to do so. Ordained priest in 1546, he twice served at the Council of Trent as theologian to Cardinal Otto Truchsess of Augsburg.

Sent into the German lands as the Reformation advanced, he taught at Ingolstadt and Vienna, preached in the cathedral of Saint Stephen, governed his order's Upper German province, and founded colleges from Vienna and Prague to Fribourg, where he settled in 1580. His three catechisms — the great Summa of 1555 with two shorter forms for students and children — passed through some two hundred editions in his lifetime and earned him the name of Second Apostle of Germany.

He died at Fribourg on 21 December 1597; beatified in 1864, he was canonized by Pius XI in 1925 and at the same time declared a Doctor of the Church. The tireless catechist is the patron of Germany and of catechists.
saints.knownFor: His catechisms and the defense of the faith in Germany.

canonization.canonized: 1925 by Pope Pius XI, who declared him a Doctor of the Church
